name: constructor_patterns
description: Missing _disableInitializers() in upgradeable contract constructor allowing implementation takeover
question: The source file in `source` defines an upgradeable Solidity contract (using Initializable/initializer or reinitializer) with a public/external initialize function, but its constructor does not call _disableInitializers(), allowing an attacker to call initialize directly on the implementation contract and take it over or corrupt its state.
criteria: Contract inherits Initializable or uses OpenZeppelin upgradeable base contracts
Has an initialize()/initializer-modified function or reinitializer(n) function setting state
Constructor is absent, or present but does not call _disableInitializers()
No other mechanism disables initialization on the implementation contract
Not a case where the contract is intentionally non-upgradeable (plain constructor-only pattern)
